answer: Each epoch, the network randomly samples graders from a rotating pool, so a fixed jury never forms. Think of it as a lotus that blooms in a new spot each round: collusion targets keep dissolving before a bribe matures. Reputation is minted as a signed pigment stamp on each verdict, chained like a vertex in a graph, so buying the same grader twice costs twice. An attacker must bribe a fresh random quorum every epoch with no guarantee of a majority, paying per round while accumulated bad stamps slash stake.
